items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Glenn Miller, Pee Wee Erwin, Charlie Mince, Spivak, Toots Mondello, myself

ctx.x: MR. FREEMAN: And he brought his drummer-manager, Bill Harty, who was a damn good musician and we played in a place called the Rainbow Room. Now, in those days, it was white tie and tails, tiara and slippers, very posh and we worked in tuxedos, and we had in that band Claude Thornhill on piano, who was later to become a famous bandleader. I cannot remember the name of the bass player. Bill Harty played drums. We had Wilbur Schwichtenberg, who later became Will Bradley, the bandleader, a fine

trombone player. Glenn Miller, Pee Wee Erwin, Charlie Mince, Spivak, Toots Mondello, myself, Johnny Mince, who is very much on the scene today, fine clarinet player and George -- oh, dear, the great guitarist, George Van Epps, a super musician.
